findings.finding: The FY26 Q4 implied by the unchanged plan is conservative. After a Q3 cumulative OP of 6,150 (+22%; Q3 alone +39%, 2,315), the 7,700 plan needs only 1,550 in Q4 (+19% on last year's 1,299). Applying last year's Q4/Q3 seasonal ratio (0.78) gives a Q4 of about 1.8bn and a FY OP of about 7.9-8.0bn: +3% on the plan, +1% on IFIS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last time this line surprised on its own was the Q3 print on 2026-07-13, when the quarter beat with the plan held, and the stock rose +8.35% the next day (Yahoo chart). At the FY25 full-year print the result beat IFIS by 1.6% and the stock still fell 5.66% (2025-10-15).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: IFIS already sits at 7,850 OP, above the plan. What is left is the gap between a seasonal-ratio estimate (~7.95bn) and 7.85bn, about 1%. If the market had fully priced the run-rate rather than the plan, IFIS would sit nearer 8.0bn.
findings.independence: kabuyoho/IFIS consensus above plan (https://kabuyoho.jp/reportAnalyst?bcode=7085). The Q3 deck and the 3-month figures share one company data source.

findings.finding: Returns set-up: the FY26 dividend is 30 yen, of which 10 yen is a one-off 20th-anniversary commemorative. Under the company's stated 50% target payout (Q3 deck), FY27 EPS in the low 60s implies an ordinary dividend of about 30 yen, so the dividend is held without the commemorative. A 3.5bn buyback (3m shares) completed on 2026-08-25, which gives precedent for a new one at a full-year print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-04-14 (H1 print with a dividend hike to 30 yen, an expanded 優待 and an upward revision; the 3.5bn buyback is in the same Q3 deck): +15.07%. The FY25 print (2025-10-15) carried no new buyback and fell 5.66%.
findings.why_not_priced: The 50% payout target is public, but a 3.15% yield on a 30-yen dividend that is one-third commemorative leaves a risk that the market reads FY27 as a dividend cut to ~20-25 yen. A guide that holds 30 yen removes that risk. If the hold were priced, the stock would trade as a durable 3.1% yielder, and nothing visible separates the two readings. A new buyback is unknowable in advance.

findings.finding: Last year's equivalent full-year print set FY26 ordinary at 7,250, 7.4% above IFIS (6,750), and the stock still fell 5.66% the next day after running from ~700 to 853 into it. This year the stock carries a similar run-in: +7.7% over 20d, +5.3% over 5d, +2.7% intraday on the day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: New-year guide prints: 2025-10-15 -5.66% (guide above consensus, after a run-up); 2024-10-16 +1.18%.
findings.why_not_priced: Pre-print positioning is visible in the run-up, which the baseline lean already reads at -0.39. This adds only the name-specific precedent that a guide above consensus was sold. If the risk were fully priced, the run-in would not have continued into the session of the release.
findings.independence: Yahoo daily closes (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/7085.T?range=3y&interval=1d) confirm the 2025-10-14/15 path (830 to 783).

findings.finding: Management has said twice since July that the 2030 vision (OP 10.3bn yen, sales 56bn yen) may be reached a year early: in the Q3 deck on 2026-07-13 and in the 2026-08-25 press release. A full-year print is the natural place to restate or raise the vision, and a raise would anchor FY27 above the ~10% CAGR path.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The vision was first published with the FY25 print on 2025-10-14, and the next day the stock fell 5.66%.
findings.why_not_priced: The statement is public, but it is qualitative. A one-analyst name has no street FY27-FY29 path, so a quantified upgrade would be new. If the market already held it, the 1,370 target (+44%) would not sit so far above spot.
findings.independence: Same claim in the Q3 deck, https://pdf.irpocket.com/C7085/xoA3/SFxs/WeSf/GmN6.pdf. It is the same company source, so it counts once.

findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The filing is public, and the +0.05pt change is tiny.

baseline_tension: Mild positive against a mildly negative lean (-0.53, all run-up). The strongest positive the release could carry is a held ~30 yen dividend under the 50% payout policy, plus a new buyback or a vision upgrade. I looked for both and could not confirm either in advance. The strongest negative is last year's identical set-up (run-up, guide above consensus, -5.7%).
lessons_applied: Open question 4 (a five-day run-in sized as a short; one case went wrong at +8.15%): the run-up/precedent negative shrank from -0.6 to -0.4.
Rule 1 (a negative on a public series): no 月次-based negative was filed, so it moved nothing.
Rule 2 (negatives outnumber positives): mine do not. I wrote the strongest positive into baseline_tension, and p_up stays at 52.
